false_positives.candidate:
Shared queue pool is shut down on strategy close (rebalance) and then reused/dropped
The FixedQueuePool is created once in the factory __init__ and shared by every strategy from create_with_partitions. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate()/join() call queue_pool.shutdown(), which shuts the queues down and stops the worker threads. On a Kafka rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy and calls create_with_partitions again, which asserts/uses the same (now dead) pool. Subsequent submit() calls hit queue.ShutDown on put(); SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches it and marks the offset added+completed, so the unprocessed message is later committed as if processed.

Probabilistic distribution assertion with randomized string hash
get_queue_for_group uses hash(str), which is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED). Asserting 20 keys hit all 3 queues fails with ~0.1% probability on random runs.

Unbounded queues: no backpressure despite documented guarantee
Queues are unbounded queue.Queue() and poll()/submit never raise MessageRejected, so the consumer keeps pulling from Kafka regardless of worker speed. A slow processor causes unbounded memory growth, contrary to the 'natural backpressure' docstring.

Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
The commit function is the StreamProcessor's commit callback. It stages offsets on the Kafka consumer, which is not thread-safe, and it is meant to be called from the main processing thread. Calling it from the daemon commit thread races with poll/stage/commit in the main thread. It can also be invoked for partitions that have since been revoked, or after the strategy is closed, which causes errors or commits for partitions the consumer no longer owns. No revocation handling clears the tracker's state for lost partitions.

Non-contiguous Kafka offsets stall commits permanently
Committable offset advances only while every integer offset in the range was seen via add_offset. Kafka offsets can have gaps (transaction control records, compaction), and Arroyo never delivers them. Once a gap occurs, the loop breaks at the gap forever, nothing past it is committed, and all_offsets grows unbounded.

Worker exits without draining queue on shutdown
FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before calling q.shutdown(immediate=False). The worker loop checks `while not self.shutdown` after each item, so it exits after at most one more item and does not drain the queue. This contradicts the intended graceful shutdown. Items already queued are never processed, and their offsets are never committed, so they are reprocessed after restart. The shutdown flag is also set before the get() unblocks, which makes the behaviour inconsistent.

Commit invoked from a background thread
The Arroyo commit callable is called from the strategy's commit thread while the StreamProcessor main thread polls/stages offsets. Arroyo's commit and the Kafka consumer's offset-staging state are not documented as thread-safe, risking races or errors in commit.

Submit failure marks offset as completed, causing it to be committed unprocessed
Any exception in submit (including failure in queue_pool.submit/put) results in the offset being added and completed, making it committable. A message that was never processed is then committed and lost.
